content: Emergency contraceptive availability varies significantly by country, with differences in access, regulations, and formulations. Below is a detailed description of the availability and regulations surrounding emergency contraceptives (EC) in various countries: Europe Finland In 1987, the Yuzpe regimen was introduced under the name Neoprimavlar. By 2002, a levonorgestrel-only emergency contraceptive (NorLevo 750 µg) became available over the counter in pharmacies. However, it cannot be administered to individuals under 15 years of age, and only one package can be purchased at a time. Recently, the two-dose NorLevo 750 µg package has been replaced by a single-dose NorLevo 1.5 mg package. France NorLevo, a two-dose progestin-only treatment, was approved in 1999 and made available without a prescription through pharmacies. However, France does not have an over-the-counter status equivalent to other countries. In December 2000, public and parochial high school nurses were authorized to dispense emergency contraceptives. Ireland In Ireland, emergency contraceptives are available without restrictions but are not sold over the counter. Access requires a visit to a doctor or a family-planning clinic. Romania In Romania, emergency contraceptives are legally available only in pharmacies and require a medical prescription. However, it is relatively easy to purchase them without presenting such a document. United Kingdom Since 2005, the primary emergency contraceptive available over the counter in UK pharmacies has been Levonelle One Step, a single-dose progestin-only treatment. It is available to individuals aged 16 and older. North America United States Since 1999, the progestin-only Plan B (two 750 µg levonorgestrel pills) has been available with a prescription. Starting in late 2006, Plan B became available over the counter in pharmacies staffed by licensed pharmacists for women aged 18 and older. A prescription-only version remains available for women aged 17 and younger. Canada Since 2005, Plan B has been available nationwide without a prescription but requires a professional consultation with a pharmacist before purchase. Oceania New Zealand In 1996, PC4, a Yuzpe regimen, was approved for unrestricted over-the-counter access. However, the manufacturer (Schering) withdrew PC4 from the New Zealand market shortly thereafter. Australia Progestin-only emergency contraceptives, such as Postinor-2 and Levonelle-2, became available in 2002. By 2004, Postinor-2 was made available without a prescription. Asia China In 1997, Anordrin, an estrogenic steroid of the 19-Norandrostane family, was the most frequently used emergency contraceptive in China. Levonorgestrel-based emergency contraceptives are marketed under the names Yu-Ting and An-Ting. In 2002, China became the first country to register mifepristone for use as an emergency contraceptive. On August 31, 2005, nonprescription, over-the-counter access to levonorgestrel-only emergency contraceptives was approved. Sri Lanka The Family Planning Association began offering the Yuzpe regimen in 1994. Malaysia Postinor was registered in 1987. Thailand Postinor is readily available over the counter in pharmacies, including chains such as Boots. South America Argentina Progestin-only emergency contraceptive pills are available for free at all public hospitals in Buenos Aires. Chile Postinor-2, a progestin-only emergency contraceptive, became legal in 2002 following a Supreme Court battle. Wealthier Chileans could purchase it on demand from private health services, while poorer individuals served by the national health service could only access it if they were victims of sexual assault. In 2006, access to emergency contraceptives was briefly allowed for all females aged 14 and older, but this was immediately blocked by a court decision. Months later, an Appeals Court upheld a lower court decision allowing the Ministry of Health to distribute emergency contraceptives to minors without parental consent. Ecuador On May 23, 2005, after being available on the market for a couple of years, the Constitutional Court of Ecuador suspended the registration and sanitary permission of Postinor-2, which had allowed it to be provided in drug stores and hospitals. Africa South Africa A Yuzpe product called E-Gen-C became available in 1997. Kenya Postinor became available in 1997. Zambia Levonorgestrel-only emergency contraceptives, such as Lenor 72, were registered in 2002. In 2005, another levonorgestrel-only product called Pregnon was registered.
